bib.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
authors: Institute for AI Industry Research (AIR), Tsinghua University
SIA-Lab of Tsinghua AIR and ByteDance Seed
Qiying Yu (project lead; full list in Contributions)

question: How can large-scale RL on a base LLM for long chain-of-thought math reasoning be made to work reproducibly, given that the R1 report omits key details?
hypothesis: Naive GRPO suffers from entropy collapse, reward noise and instability; four targeted changes (Clip-Higher, Dynamic Sampling, token-level loss, overlong reward shaping) close the gap to DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B.
contributions: DAPO algorithm with four techniques: Clip-Higher, Dynamic Sampling, Token-Level Policy Gradient Loss, Overlong Reward Shaping
Open-source training code built on verl
DAPO-Math-17K dataset of 17K prompts with integer answers
50 points on AIME 2024 with Qwen2.5-32B base

method.summary: GRPO-style group-normalised policy gradient with no KL term and rule-based +1/-1 reward, modified by decoupled clip ranges (eps_low 0.2, eps_high 0.28), filtering of prompts whose group accuracy is 0 or 1 with oversampling, token-level loss averaging over all tokens in the group, and filtering or length-penalising truncated samples. Trained on Qwen2.5-32B base with the verl framework.
method.task: reinforcement learning for verifiable math reasoning (long CoT)

datasets.name: DAPO-Math-17K
datasets.size: 17K prompts, each with an integer answer
datasets.source: web and official competition homepages via web scraping and manual annotation; answers transformed to integers by an LLM rewriting the question
datasets.preprocessing: Select and transform answers into integers (e.g. a+sqrt(b)/c becomes a+b+c); LLM uses CoT with four steps: extract answer format, rewrite problem, solve modified problem, give integer answer, with few-shot solutions or guidelines

other.note: number (47) taken from the R1 report

training.objective: DAPO objective (Eq. 8/12): token-level clipped surrogate with eps_low 0.2 and eps_high 0.28, group-normalised advantage A=(R-mean)/std, no KL term, constraint 0 < #correct < G; reward +1 if equivalent else -1 plus soft overlong punishment
training.batch_size: rollout prompt batch 512 with 16 responses per prompt; mini-batch size 512 (16 gradient updates per rollout step)
training.steps: inferred: about 5000 gradient steps for the final run from Fig 1 and 7 axes (Fig 1 axis runs to 10000); not stated in text
training.seq_len: 16,384 expected max + 4,096 soft punish cache = 20,480 max generation tokens

other.baseline: naive GRPO with group reward normalization
other.mu_inner_iterations: Algorithm 1 mu not given numerically; inferred 16 updates per rollout step from mini-batch note

inference.samples: AIME evaluation set repeated 32 times, avg@32; Fig 1 also shows pass@32 and cons@32

metrics.name: AIME 2024 avg@32
metrics.definition: accuracy averaged over 32 repeats of the evaluation set

eval.protocol: single training run per configuration as far as stated; no seeds or significance tests reported; ablations are cumulative (Table 1)

availability.code: https://github.com/volcengine/verl (training code built on verl; project page https://dapo-sia.github.io/)

limits: Only math tasks with verifiable integer answers; transfer to other tasks is asserted not shown ('can be readily transferred to other tasks').
Single model (Qwen2.5-32B), single benchmark (AIME 2024); no seeds, error bars or significance tests; ablation is cumulative so order dependent.
Number of total training steps, hardware and compute are not stated.
Comparison to DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B uses the R1 report's number and differing setups.
Reward on train set poorly correlates with validation accuracy (overfitting) per authors.
Emergent reflection is shown by one case study, not measured.

terms.definition: decouple lower and higher clip ranges eps_low and eps_high and raise eps_high to leave room for low-probability tokens
over-sample and filter out prompts with accuracy equal to 1 and 0 so every batch has effective gradients
Overlong Filtering masks loss of truncated samples; Soft Overlong Punishment adds a length-aware penalty in an interval before max length

lineage.note: DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B scores 47 on AIME; DAPO beats it
naive GRPO is the baseline algorithm

figures.caption: AIME 2024 scores of DAPO on the Qwen2.5-32B base model, outperforming the previous SoTA DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B using 50% training steps.

code.snippet: J_DAPO = E[ 1/(sum_i |o_i|) sum_i sum_t min(r_it A_it, clip(r_it, 1-eps_low, 1+eps_high) A_it) ] s.t. 0 < |{o_i | is_equivalent(a,o_i)}| < G
R_length(y) = 0 if |y|<=Lmax-Lcache; ((Lmax-Lcache)-|y|)/Lcache if Lmax-Lcache<|y|<=Lmax; -1 if Lmax<|y|
